title: Manual model routing aliases
description: Add dashboard-managed routing aliases for models, editable from model settings and visible from a global models page.

tasks.title: Build manual alias storage and ownership helpers
tasks.description: Add a focused orchestration layer for dashboard-managed aliases inside router settings so later API and UI tasks can read/write aliases without clobbering generated plugin aliases.
acceptanceCriteria: A helper can read all manual aliases, read aliases for one target model, and return a flat alias -> target map from router_settings.
A helper can replace the manual aliases for one target model while preserving generated aliases and unrelated router_settings fields.
A helper can retarget manual aliases during model rename and report aliases blocking model deletion.
Unit tests cover preserving managed aliases, duplicate ownership metadata cleanup, rename retarget, and delete guard behavior.
requirements: The dashboard updates only manual alias keys that it owns.

steps.title: Create manual alias orchestration module
steps.description: Add a new orchestration helper that parses router_settings, separates dashboard-owned aliases from generated aliases, and exposes read/write operations for model-scoped alias editing.
steps.expectedResult: A reusable server-side module owns manual alias storage semantics.

steps.title: Implement rename and delete guard helpers
steps.description: Add helper functions that retarget aliases when a model name changes and detect aliases that block model deletion.
steps.expectedResult: Route handlers can call one helper for rename retarget and another for delete guard checks.

steps.title: Export and test the helper
steps.description: Expose the new helper from the orchestration index and add focused tests for ownership metadata and storage preservation rules.
steps.expectedResult: Focused helper tests pass and document the storage contract.

produces: export interface ManualModelAliasEntry { alias: string; targetModel: string; }
export async function listManualModelAliases(settingsService: ISettingsService): Promise<ManualModelAliasEntry[]>
export async function replaceManualAliasesForTarget(settingsService: ISettingsService, targetModel: string, aliases: string[]): Promise<ManualModelAliasEntry[]>
export async function retargetManualAliases(settingsService: ISettingsService, previousModelName: string, nextModelName: string): Promise<void>
export async function listBlockingManualAliases(settingsService: ISettingsService, targetModel: string): Promise<string[]>

notes: Preserve __lite_llm_analytics.managedModelGroupAliasKeys exactly; do not merge the manual ownership array into the generated ownership array.
Normalize and sort alias keys deterministically before writing so UI diffs remain stable.
Do not use the unused ModelProxyAlias table for this version.

tasks.title: Expose manual alias API endpoints and validations
tasks.description: Add dedicated model alias endpoints in the models API, wire server-side validations, retarget aliases on model rename, block deletion when aliases still point to the model, and provide a dedicated web client wrapper.
acceptanceCriteria: The server exposes list, target-scoped read, replace, and delete operations for manual aliases under the models API.
Alias writes reject duplicate alias keys, alias/model name collisions, missing target models, and alias-to-alias targets with actionable 4xx responses.
Renaming a model through PUT /models/:name retargets manual aliases in the same successful operation.
Deleting a model with attached manual aliases returns a blocking error instead of removing the model.
A dedicated web client module exists for manual alias endpoints and is ready for both UI surfaces.
Integration tests cover happy path CRUD plus rename/delete edge cases.
requirements: Alias key MUST be unique across all manual and generated aliases.
Alias key MUST NOT equal the name of any real model.
Alias key MUST NOT target another alias; targets must resolve to canonical model names only.
Alias mutations return actionable validation errors.

steps.title: Add manual alias route handlers
steps.description: In model-routes, add GET /models/aliases, GET /models/:name/aliases, PUT /models/:name/aliases, and DELETE /models/aliases/:alias using the new orchestration helper.
steps.expectedResult: Routes expose a dedicated API surface for manual alias management.

steps.title: Wire rename and delete guards into existing model mutations
steps.description: Update PUT /models/:name to retarget aliases after a successful rename and update DELETE /models/:name to reject deletes when manual aliases still point to the model.
steps.expectedResult: Model lifecycle operations enforce alias integrity automatically.

steps.title: Add web client wrapper and integration tests
steps.description: Create a dedicated api-client module for alias calls and cover the full server behavior with runtime-level tests.
steps.expectedResult: Server tests pass and web code can consume typed alias endpoints.

consumes: import { listManualModelAliases, replaceManualAliasesForTarget, retargetManualAliases, listBlockingManualAliases } from "@lite-llm/server/orchestration"
produces: export async function getAllModelAliases(): Promise<{ aliases: ManualModelAliasEntry[] }>
export async function getModelAliases(modelName: string): Promise<{ modelName: string; aliases: string[] }>
export async function updateModelAliases(modelName: string, aliases: string[]): Promise<{ aliases: ManualModelAliasEntry[] }>
export async function deleteModelAlias(alias: string): Promise<{ success: boolean }>

notes: Return 400-level responses for validation failures and keep 500s for unexpected errors only.
Do not piggyback on plugin-routing routes; keep alias CRUD under the models API surface.
Route-level tests should run against the real runtime wiring used by apps/server.

tasks.title: Add manual aliases editor to model settings
tasks.description: Extend the model settings flow so each model detail page can load, edit, and save the manual aliases that route to that model.
acceptanceCriteria: The model settings tab shows a manual aliases section with routing-only explanatory copy.
Operators can add, edit, and remove aliases locally before saving the model.
Saving the form writes both model settings and aliases without losing existing alias data on failure.
After save, the page refreshes and reflects the saved aliases for that model.
requirements: The model detail page exposes a manual aliases editor in the model settings flow.
The editor supports list, add, edit, and remove before save.
Aliases are routing-only and do not create model metadata of their own.

steps.title: Create reusable aliases editor component
steps.description: Add a model-aliases-editor component with add/remove rows, inline validation affordances, and copy that explains aliases are routing-only.
steps.expectedResult: The settings page has a focused UI primitive for editing aliases.

steps.title: Load and stage aliases in use-model-config-page
steps.description: Fetch aliases for the current model, store them alongside the form state, and call updateModelAliases after the main model update succeeds.
steps.expectedResult: Saving settings also persists aliases and invalidates the relevant model queries.

steps.title: Render the aliases editor in the settings form
steps.description: Mount the new editor in model-config-form and reflect dirty state when aliases change.
steps.expectedResult: Focused web tests pass or are extended for the settings flow.

produces: Manual aliases section in the model settings form.
Form state that includes staged alias values for the current model.

notes: If alias save fails after model settings save succeeds, surface a clear toast and keep the page refresh path predictable.
Do not inject alias rows into the main model route payload; alias persistence uses its dedicated endpoint.
Keep copy explicit that aliases affect routing names only.

tasks.title: Add global manual aliases page under models
tasks.description: Create a global models-area view that lists manual aliases, supports search and target filtering, and lets operators remove aliases without opening each model detail page.
acceptanceCriteria: A new /models/aliases page renders a searchable list of manual aliases and their target models.
The page supports filtering by target model and removing an alias from the table.
Navigation exposes the page from the models section without moving alias management into plugins.
Removing an alias refreshes the list and leaves model detail data consistent.
requirements: The global aliases view is placed in the models area, not in plugins.
The global aliases API response returns a flat list of manual alias entries with alias and targetModel.
The global view supports search by alias and filter by target model.

steps.title: Create the global aliases page
steps.description: Build a models page with table/search/filter/remove interactions backed by the dedicated alias client module.
steps.expectedResult: Operators can review and remove aliases from one place.

steps.title: Register route and navigation
steps.description: Add the new route in App.tsx and a sidebar entry under models so the page is discoverable alongside configured models, credentials, and health checks.
steps.expectedResult: The aliases page is reachable in the existing models navigation cluster.

steps.title: Verify page behavior
steps.description: Run focused web tests or add a lightweight page test if the route tree needs coverage for aliases navigation.
steps.expectedResult: Focused UI coverage passes for aliases listing and removal flows.

produces: Sidebar entry in the models section for aliases

notes: Keep the page in the models area even if plugin alias tables already exist elsewhere.
Use model names from the alias payload for filter options rather than fetching a second dataset unless the UI needs richer labels.
Removal should confirm intent or otherwise make the destructive action clearly labeled.
